document.title: Answer of Silver Run Electric, LLC to the 02/20/2025 Order Instituting Proceeding Under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act

pages.text:
March 24, 2025 
 
The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Esq. 
Secretary 
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission 
888 First Street, N.E. 
Washington, DC 20426 
 
 
Re: 
Silver Run Electric, LLC, Docket Nos. EL25-49-000, AD24-11-000, EL25-20-000 
Response to the Commission’s Order Instituting Proceeding under Section 206 of the Federal 
Power Act  
 
Dear Secretary Reese: 
 
Pursuant to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission” or “FERC”) February 20, 
2025 order issued in the above-captioned proceeding,1 Silver Run Electric, LLC (“Silver Run”), as PJM 
Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) Transmission Owner, respectfully submits this response in accordance 
with the Commission’s directive and explains that it takes no position on the matters that the 
Commission raises in its order.  Silver Run commits to working with PJM, the other PJM Transmission 
Owners, and the other stakeholders in this proceeding as necessary to implement any Tariff changes 
that may be required as part of this proceeding. 
 
 
I. 
BACKGROUND 
The February 20 Order instituted a proceeding under section 206 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 
wherein the Commission directed PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners to show cause as to why the 
PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff, Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of PJM, and 
Reliability Assurance Agreement Among Load Serving Entities in the PJM Region (collectively, the 
“Tariff”) (a) remains just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential with regards to 
the rates, terms, and conditions of service applying to co-location arrangements or (b) explain what 
changes would remedy the Commission’s identified concerns if FERC were to determine the Tariff has 
become unjust and unreasonable or unduly discriminatory or preferential and, therefore, establishes a 
replacement Tariff. 
 
Silver Run is an electric transmission-only utility company established to develop, own, and operate 
transmission facilities within the PJM region, and is organized under the laws of the State of Delaware.  
Silver Run is an indirect subsidiary of LS Power Associates, L.P.  Silver Run owns and operates discrete 
and limited transmission facilities.  Specifically, Silver Run owns and operates one substation in New 
 
1  
See PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., et al., 190 FERC ¶ 61,115 (2025) (“February 20 Order”).

2/3 
Castle County, Delaware (the Silver Run Substation) and a 5.5-mile, 230 kV transmission line, which 
includes an approximately 3-mile submarine crossing of the Delaware River, connecting the Silver Run 
Substation to the Hope Creek Nuclear Plant Switchyard located in Salem County, New Jersey.  Silver 
Run built these transmission assets as part of PJM’s Order No. 1000-compliant competitive solicitation 
process associated with the Artificial Island Project, which was needed to improve transmission system 
performance in the area.2  These transmission assets, which commenced operations on April 28, 2020, 
were the first and, thus far, only transmission assets owned by Silver Run. 
 
II. 
RESPONSE 
Silver Run has carefully reviewed each of the issues raised in the February 20 Order, including the 
briefing questions reflected in Section VI.D of the February 20 Order.  Silver Run, however, is asserting 
no position in this proceeding but is committed to working alongside PJM, the other PJM Transmission 
Owners, and other stakeholders in this proceeding to implement any related Tariff changes that the 
Commission may require to be made. 
 
Silver Run is taking no position on this matter, because it is a PJM Transmission Owner with no 
service territory, no load, and no generator interconnection customers, pending or otherwise.  
Furthermore, as explained above, Silver Run’s sole assets are transmission facilities under PJM’s 
operational control.  Consequently, if and when any load or generator customers seek to interconnect 
to Silver Run’s transmission facilities, co-located or not, PJM will oversee the processing thereof, and 
Silver Run will abide by any Tariff provisions effective at that time. 
 
III. 
CONCLUSION 
Silver Run looks forward to the opportunity of working with the Commission, its staff, PJM, and 
other stakeholders in this proceeding on any Tariff revisions that the Commission may find are 
necessary.  Please contact the undersigned with any questions regarding this filing. 
 
  
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
/s/Blake R. Urban 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Blake R. Urban 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Seth Yeazel 
LS Power Development, LLC 
 
2  
In 2013, PJM selected Northeast Transmission Development, LLC’s (“Northeast Transmission”) proposal to improve 
operational performance and reliability in the Artificial Island area.  In 2018, Northeast Transmission merged with 
Silver Run.  The Commission accepted Silver Run’s Notice of Succession and corresponding changes to the Intra-
PJM Tariffs.  PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Docket No. ER18-1983-000 (Aug. 24, 2018) (delegated letter order).  
Furthermore, on October 26, 2022, the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities selected Silver Run to expand its 
existing project as part of PJM’s State Agreement Approach, to facilitate the successful delivery of offshore wind to 
New Jersey customers.  Order on the State Agreement Approach SAA Proposals, Docket No. QO20100630 (N.J. Bd. 
of Pub. Util., Oct. 26, 2022).
